body:
## What is needed

Many users receive 2D drawings as `.dwg` files. DWG is a closed binary format, so CamCraft should not write a native DWG reader or bundle non-commercial converters.

## Design

- Document "save as DXF in your CAD program" as the primary, zero-risk workflow.
- Add an optional external-process integration in `crates/app` that detects a user-installed LibreDWG `dwg2dxf` binary on `PATH` (or at a user-configured path):
  - Never link LibreDWG into CamCraft and never bundle its binary in installers (GPLv3 separation).
  - Never default to ODA File Converter (non-commercial restriction for non-members and no third-party redistribution).
  - Run `dwg2dxf` in a temporary directory with a strict timeout and output byte cap, passing only the file arguments (no shell invocation).
  - Feed the resulting `.dxf` bytes through the existing fuzz-tested `ImportDxf` reader (`crates/app/src/commands/import_dxf.rs`) with all existing unit refusals and limits.
  - Display both converter warnings and CamCraft's DXF skipped-entity summary so lost entities are never silent.
- Refuse cleanly with actionable guidance ("install `dwg2dxf` or save as DXF") when `dwg2dxf` is absent, exits non-zero, or times out.

Clean-room rule: external process invocation only; untrusted converter output passes through CamCraft's own DXF reader.

**Done means:** importing a `.dwg` runs user-installed `dwg2dxf` with a timeout, routes output through `ImportDxf` with skipped-entity reporting, refuses cleanly when `dwg2dxf` is missing or fails, and passes unit tests with a mock converter binary without bundling GPL code.

## What is needed

Machinists working from a paper print often need to enter a custom 2D profile as an ordered list of lines and arcs where some intermediate endpoints are defined by tangency, angle, or intersection rather than explicit XY coordinates.

## Design

- Add a pure 2D contour solver in `camcraft-geometry` that accepts an ordered list of typed segments:
  - Line (endpoint, length, angle, tangent to previous/next arc, or intersection with adjacent segment).

- Solve exact analytic intersections and tangent points (line-line, line-circle, circle-circle) from published 2D analytic geometry.
- Refuse under-constrained, over-constrained, non-intersecting, or ambiguous multi-solution joins by segment index with a clear diagnostic; require an explicit branch selector when two geometric solutions exist. Never guess a branch silently.
- Compile the solved contour into a normal `Sketch` (`SketchData` primitives) with its typed segment list persisted in `.camproj`, editable via an undoable command, and exposed through MCP.

Clean-room rule: standard 2D analytic geometry only. Do not copy vendor UI layouts, parameter names, or solver code.

**Done means:** a closed contour mixing lines, explicit arcs, tangent arcs, and computed intersections solves to analytic primitives, refuses ambiguous joins by name, round-trips `.camproj`, undoes cleanly, and generates a verified `2D Contour`.

## What is needed

CamCraft has turning operations (`Facing`, `ProfileRough`, `ProfileFinish`, `GrooveRough`, `GrooveFinish`, `Threading`, `Part`, `Chamfering`, `TaperTurning`, `BoringTurning`), but `sketch_model::admits` (`crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`) admits only `Mill2D`, `Plasma`, and `WireEdm`. Turning currently requires a revolved 3D mesh (`crates/app/src/operation/turning_outline.rs`).

## Design

- Add a parametric turned half-profile representation in `camcraft-geometry` built from a step table in `(r, z)` coordinates (outer or inner profile: diameter, axial length or Z station, taper angle, corner chamfer or radius, and groove/thread relief).
- Follow the clean-room half-profile conventions already established for `SpunProfile` (`docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`) while keeping workpiece profiles distinct from tool holders.
- Refuse invalid step tables by name: non-finite values, negative radii, self-intersecting steps, impossible corner blends, or axial reversals where disallowed.
- Admit this profile source for `Section::Turning` in `sketch_model`, derive the revolved silhouette and stock verification envelope without requiring a 3D STL/STEP mesh, and persist it in `.camproj`.
- Add undoable commands (`CreateTurnProfile`, `EditTurnProfile`) and MCP tools.

Clean-room rule: use standard lathe geometry terms from machining handbooks (Smid, *CNC Programming Handbook*; *Machinery's Handbook*). Do not copy vendor parameter names or layouts.

**Safety floor:** new geometry source feeding turning toolpaths and collision verification (`effort:max`).

**Done means:** a stepped shaft half-profile validates, refuses invalid tables by name, round-trips `.camproj`, undoes cleanly, and provides verified turning bounds without a 3D mesh.

body:
## What is needed

Shop-floor users who run quick-op contours, bosses, frames, and pocket finish passes expect to adjust part size slightly at the machine control using the tool wear offset register (`G41`/`G42`).

## Design

- Default quick-op finishing contours, bosses, and frames to `Compensation::Wear` (`crates/motion/src/approach.rs`) when the active post supports cutter compensation.
- In `Compensation::Wear`, CamCraft writes the cutter-centre path under `G41`/`G42` so the part cuts to nominal size when the control wear register is zero.
- Keep `Compensation::Computer` automatically when:
  - The active post does not support `G41`/`G42`.
  - The operation cuts an open chain (`crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch.rs`).
- Seed valid linear lead-in and lead-out lengths (at least one cutter radius, per RS-274 / ISO 6983 startup and cancel rules) so the existing lead refusal law is satisfied by default, and keep the refusal active if the user shortens the lead.
- Allow the user to switch the operation to `Computer` or `Control` in the normal parameter panel or via MCP.

Clean-room rule: based on RS-274 / ISO 6983 cutter radius compensation rules and existing `Compensation::Wear` behaviour.

**Safety floor:** changes posted `G41`/`G42` G-code and lead validation (`effort:high`).

**Done means:** a quick-op finishing contour posts `G41`/`G42` wear compensation on Fanuc, Haas, and LinuxCNC posts, falls back to `Computer` on posts without cutter compensation, refuses short leads by name, and is pinned by golden post tests.

body:
Requested by a Discord user (PR-FPV), relayed by mkinney 2026-11-21. He runs **FluidNC** on a **PiBot** controller board on a **3040** hobby router.

## What is missing
CamCraft has Grbl, grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera posts, but no FluidNC post and no 3040-class machine file. FluidNC is grbl-derived but has its own G/M-code coverage and configuration (YAML), so the Grbl post is a guess on it.

## Clean-room sources (only these)
- FluidNC's own public documentation (wiki.fluidnc.com: supported G-codes and M-codes, tool change, spindle and coolant, probing, the YAML config).
- What the owner's FluidNC machine accepts on a dry run.
- **Never** another CAM product's post or its output. The owner made a working post for himself with an AI from his Vectric Aspire post; that file must not be used or read for this issue.

## What to decide from the docs
- Program start and end, units, the safe start line.
- Tool change: `M6` support versus a stop (FluidNC can run a tool-change macro); what to write for a machine without ATC.
- Spindle (`M3`/`M5`, `S`), coolant (`M7`/`M8`/`M9`), canned cycles (written out as moves if unsupported), arcs, probing (`G38.x`).
- Which differences from `grbl.cps` matter; reuse its structure where FluidNC behaves the same.

## Machine file
A generic 3040 router (about 300 x 400 mm work area, small spindle): `kind` mill, no ATC, travel and spindle range stated as typical and marked for the owner to confirm.

Done means: a built-in `FluidNC` post and a `3040` machine file ship; conformance and golden tests pin the output; each dialect decision names its FluidNC documentation page in `docs/decisions/`; the header says not verified on a machine until the owner reports a clean dry run.

body:
`gate batch` runs one `cargo test -p <crate> --no-run` prebuild for each crate (`#2727`) so later per-crate suite steps reuse the exact feature resolution.

In `batch-20261121-112020/0[1-9]-debug_build_*.log`, per-crate feature divergence caused repeated recompilation inside one warm batch run:
- `01-debug_build_geometry`: compiled `kernel`, `geometry` (6 s).
- `02-debug_build_kernel`: compiled `kernel` with `truck` dev-feature (4 s, expected).
- `05-debug_build_post`: recompiled `kernel`, `geometry`, `cl`, and `post` (15.7 s).
- `08-debug_build_app`: recompiled 6 third-party crates (`ring`, `rustls`, `reqwest`, ...) plus `kernel`, `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, and `app` (169 s).
- `09-debug_build_ui`: recompiled 10 third-party crates (`spade`, `tracing-subscriber`, `num`, `solidcore-tess`, `reqwest`, ...) plus `kernel` through `app` and `ui` (58.9 s).

One batch run compiled `kernel` 5 times, `geometry` and `cl` 4 times, `tools`/`post`/`sim`/`motion` 3 times, and `app` 2 times. This adds ~40–60 s to every warm batch run and multiplies unit variants in `target/debug/build/`.

Identify the diverging optional dependency features across `crates/*/Cargo.toml` (using `cargo tree -e features`) and align the workspace dependency feature declarations so `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, and `ui` share one compiled rlib per lower crate during `gate batch`.

Evidence and measurements: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/919#issuecomment-7065686766

Done means: in a warm `cargo xtask gate batch` run, each workspace library crate (`geometry` through `app`) compiles once across the 9 prebuild steps (only `kernel` repeats for its `truck` dev-feature), verified from the `01..09` build logs.

- `xtask/src/assets.rs:48` reads only `crates/<d>/tests/{b}.rs`. Folding any post or machine test into a directory suite breaks `#923` asset selection.
- `xtask/src/catalog.rs:146` checks `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` instead of `suites::entry(root, "app", "example_catalog")`.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs:181` (`may_run_ignored`) returns `true` whenever `mod x;` appears in `main.rs`, so every directory suite gets a heavy step even without `#[ignore]` tests.
- `xtask/src/quick.rs:186-195` (`map_modules`) merges Gate maps across all submodules of a directory suite and runs the whole binary (`p.whole`). Editing helper code inside one submodule also runs the whole binary (`quick.rs:103-133`).

Fall back to the whole binary only when `main.rs` or a shared module changes.

body:
A small, separate slice of the post-merge work. #2908 (lanes, claimed by the maintainer) stays as it is. Proposed in the mkinney comments on #2908 of 2026-11-21.

## What happens now

`post-merge.yml` uses one concurrency group for `main` (`post-merge-main`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). One run at a time; a second push waits, and a third push cancels the waiting one. A merge batch costs cancelled runs, and a red run covers several merges, so finding the breaking merge needs a bisect (#3111 took hours).

## Wanted

1. One concurrency group per commit: `post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Each push runs on its own free `camcraft-post-merge` runner and always finishes; nothing waits behind another run and nothing is cancelled. The `gate` job does not change. With today's two runners (wopr, uma) two merges are gated at once; more runners only add capacity.
2. Results can now finish out of order. The `report` job gets its own concurrency group (`post-merge-report`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) and a full-history checkout. `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` keeps the last reported commit in a hidden marker in the rolling issue body (`<!-- post-merge-last-sha: <sha> -->`) and skips (notice only) a run whose commit is an ancestor of that sha and not equal to it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). No new secrets or repository variables.
3. An xtask test (like `xtask/tests/post_merge_report.rs`) pins: the per-commit group, `cancel-in-progress: false`, and the report skipping an older commit.

This is a workflow change: the maintainer decides (the review labels it `needs-maintainer`).

Done means: two pushes in a row each get a full post-merge run that finishes (neither is cancelled); a red run names exactly its own commit; an older green run never closes the rolling issue that a newer red run opened (pinned by the xtask test).

Part of #617. Machine data from a Sodick owner (spikeypineapple, **Sodick AQ600L**, LN control): the machine's condition table, exported as `COND.DAT` and posted on #617 ([COND.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35214655/COND.txt), 68 KB, CRLF, unchanged). Machine data, not another CAM's output, so it is usable under the clean-room rules.

## What the table is

- 900 lines `Cnnn = f1 ... f15;`, quoted, CRLF. Header comment names the 15 fields: `ON OFF IP HRP MAO SV V SF C PIK CTRL WK WT WS WP`.
- Comment lines group the conditions by material, wire diameter and cut:

| Conditions | Section (as written in the file) |
|---|---|
| C100-C136 | WATER, SKD-11, wire 0.2 mm |
| C200-C230 | water, SKD-11, wire 0.25 mm |
| C400-C414 / C450-C479 | water, WC (carbide), wire 0.20 / 0.25 mm |
| C700-C719 / C750-C764 | water, AL, wire 0.20 / 0.25 mm |
| C800-C822 / C850-C867 | water, Cu, wire 0.20 / 0.25 mm |
| C480-C595 | 1st cut sets by wire (0.1 / 0.2 mm) and material (SKD11, WC) |
| C300-C395 | BS2, 2nd cut |
| C908-C938 / C909-C999 | BS2I-PKA, 3rd / 4th cut |
| C777, C888, C890-C893 | special (NEW4400 block) |

- `C120` appears twice with the same values.

## Why it matters now

Our post writes fixed condition numbers. The owner confirms that `C001` and `C002` **do** exist on his machine and are used for almost every pass, even though `COND.DAT` lists only `C100` and up. So the low numbers (`C000`-`C099`) come from somewhere else: written in the program, copied from this table into a working set, or a separate table. Asked on #617; his hand-written known-good program should show it. This issue must not assume a condition is missing just because it is not in `COND.DAT`.

## Wanted

- Read a `COND.DAT` (this format) into a condition library: number, the 15 fields, and the section it sits in (material, wire diameter, cut stage).
- The Sodick wire operation picks the rough and skim conditions from that library by material, wire diameter and pass, instead of fixed numbers; the post writes those numbers.
- A condition the loaded table and the working set (C000-C099, see above) both lack is refused by name before posting - only once we know where the working set comes from.
- Without a loaded table, today's behaviour stays (the header warns that each C must exist on the control).

The meaning of each field (IP, SV, WT ...) is not needed to pick by section; do not guess units for them. Ask the owner on #617 before adding his file to the repo as a test fixture; until then, a small synthetic file in the same format is enough for the tests.

Done means: a `COND.DAT` in this format loads (a test with a synthetic file in the same format, CRLF and quotes included); the 2-pass Sodick program picks its conditions from the loaded table by material, wire and pass; a condition missing from both the table and the working set is refused by name; with no table the output is byte-identical to today.

title: 2D Chamfer: select a minimum cone radius for the cut

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Wanted

A 2D Chamfer can state a minimum cone radius. The cone then cuts the requested chamfer through a radial band above that radius.

This lets the user keep the selected edge and the requested chamfer width. For example, a 6 mm chamfer mill can cut a 1 mm chamfer at a 2 mm minimum cone radius. The cutting band is then 2 mm to 3 mm from the tool axis.

## Current behaviour

CamCraft places the virtual cone tip on the selected wall. It keeps the tip at:

```text
tip_z = top_z - width * tan(angle)
```

The tool centre has no XY offset from the picked line. A larger chamfer mill therefore cuts through the smallest part of its cone. The operation has no setting that moves to a larger-radius band of the same cone.

## Proposed rule

For an ideal sharp cone, add one operation value named `Minimum cone radius`.

```text
minimum cone radius = r
chamfer width = w
centreline offset toward air = r
tip_z = top_z - (r + w) * tan(chamfer angle)
contact radius = r to r + w
```

For a 45-degree chamfer, a 6 mm tool, `w = 1 mm`, and `r = 2 mm`:

```text
centreline offset = 2 mm
contact radius = 2 mm to 3 mm
tip_z = top_z - 3 mm
```

The final chamfer stays 1 mm wide. The tool uses a 2 mm to 3 mm part of the cone instead of its 0 mm to 1 mm part.

The `Side` setting determines the air side for closed rings and selected open chains.

## Safety doors

- Refuse when `r` is negative or not finite.
- Refuse when the tool radius is smaller than `r + width`.
- Refuse when the cone or flute reach cannot supply `(r + width) * tan(angle)`.
- Offset closed loops and open chains with the same air-side law.
- Refuse an offset that folds, disappears, or reaches material on the air side.
- Keep the declared `EdgeBreak` on the original picked edge with the authored width and depth. The larger contact band must not create credit for more edge work.
- Stock simulation and collision verification must judge the offset cone position, not the old tip-on-wall position.

## Scope

This issue does not model or compensate for tool-tip wear. It selects a band of the current ideal sharp cone.

Issue #895 is related because it tracks real flat, ball, and radiused tip geometry. This operation-level feature can be specified independently.

## Done means

- The Geometry page exposes `Minimum cone radius` for a 2D Chamfer.
- The value round-trips through project files and the MCP operation parameter surface.
- A 45-degree, 6 mm ideal cone cuts an authored 1 mm chamfer with a 2 mm minimum radius.
- A test proves the contact radii are 2 mm and 3 mm, and the tip path is 3 mm below the top plane.
- A motion test proves a closed ring offsets toward the side `Side` names.
- A motion test proves each selected open chain offsets toward its air side.
- The tool-radius and flute-reach refusals name the missing dimension.
- Stock simulation proves the final 1 mm edge break and no gouge on the part.
- Existing 0 mm-minimum-radius projects keep the current path byte for byte.

## Labels

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, and `effort:high`.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer can use a selected larger-radius band of a chamfer mill while preserving the authored chamfer width.

body:
## What is missing

We want to post a CamCraft milling job as a conversational Heidenhain Klartext (`.H`) program. Our first target is a Fehlmann Picomax 55 with an iTNC 530 running NC software `340490-03`. CamCraft already writes Heidenhain DIN/ISO programs. Issue #3095 tests that post. Issue #2227 proposes a reader for Klartext files. This proposal concerns the writer.

## Proposed design

- Add one **Heidenhain Klartext** post alongside the DIN/ISO post. Keep the implementation, machine data, and test fixtures in CamCraft.
- Let the machine definition identify the installed control, its NC software, and its tool-change procedure. Record installed options when a supported feature needs them.
- Let the post select the documented syntax for that combination. For example, the Picomax needs a manual tool change with the quill at its physical change position. Other iTNC 530 machines can have a different tool changer.
- Start with one metric setup, three linear axes, stock bounds, preset selection, straight moves, plunges, and constant-height XY arcs. Refuse unsupported operations by name. Drilling cycles, tapping, probing, and tilted planes can have separate acceptance criteria later.

## What the local prototype shows

The prototype has one output implementation. It accepts the exact model and release above. Changing only the configured release to `340490-04` or `606425-04` makes it refuse the job before writing a file.

We ran two CamCraft programs on the Heidenhain iTNC 530 programming station, NC software `606425-04 SP20`. Its converter accepted all 41 blocks of a single-tool contour and all 63 blocks of a two-tool program. Test Run reached all three and five programmed stops, respectively. Both runs reached the end of the program without a logged NC error.

This supports those two programs on the station release. Acceptance on the physical `340490-03` installation remains open. Cycle 247 does not activate the preset during Test Run. Preset activation, quill clearance, and physical coolant operation still need checks on the machine. [HEIDENHAIN manuals for NC software 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/html/en/index/1242135142456/1242135142480/1242135142485/1242135142485.html)

## Questions for the maintainers

1. Should the first release require an exact NC software match? When two releases document the same feature, what evidence should let them share the same output?
2. Which facts belong in the existing machine definition, and which should CamCraft maintain for each supported control? Tool-change behavior and supported cycle parameters are the first cases we would use to check that boundary.
3. Would one bounded draft PR suit the project? We propose to rework the local prototype after agreement, then submit the machine definition, post, golden output, and refusal tests together. We can split the machine-data changes first if that is easier to review. We would include the manual references, station results, and outstanding machine checks in the PR.

**Done means:** The maintainers record whether to proceed, the first supported scope, the evidence required, and the preferred PR split. We will wait for that decision before submitting code.

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `needs-research`, `area:post`, `P8`, `effort:high`, `source:agent`.

Whether AGENTS.md's reference list should name "public feature lists of other products, for gap finding only" is a question for the maintainer.

**Open questions**
1. Which conversational operations are common across systems (mill and lathe)? A table: operation, which systems have it, what inputs it needs in machining terms.
2. Which of those CamCraft already covers (existing operations that would work from a sketch or stock alone), which need only a new "from numbers" front end, and which are genuinely new toolpath work?
3. Where does it live: a "quick op" that makes its own sketch geometry and a normal operation (undoable commands + MCP tools), versus a separate wizard? Recommendation needed.
4. Output style: canned cycles and cutter comp where the post supports them (conversational users expect short, readable programs) versus expanded moves.
5. Priority order for sub-issues, by how many users it helps.

Part of #1445. Found during the fine boring work (#1479).

- Mach4: `G76`. Read the word layout from the Mach4 Mill G-code manual before any word is written.
- LinuxCNC, PathPilot, grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera: no fine boring cycle. They continue to refuse.

Also owed:

- A row for `spindle.orientation` on the Machines sheet, as for `Rigid tapping`.
- `spindle.orientation` stated in the shipped machine files, where the maker's public data says it.
- A literature check of the Haas `G76` block (`I`, `J`, `P`) against the Haas Mill Operator's Manual. The session that wrote it had no web access.

Safety: a post writes the cycle only with a shift direction that the program states or that the machine file states. A post never writes a plain bore in place of a fine bore.

body:
Standardize 3D `Deburr` on chamfer chord width `w`, add Constant Depth sizing, and support multi-pass edge breaks.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr.rs` (`DeburrParams`)
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs` (`deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte`)
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`, `sane.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs`
- `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` (`PROJECT_VERSION`), `crates/app/src/mcp/`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`

## What to change

1. Redefine `DeburrParams.width` and `OpParams::Deburr.width` as chamfer chord width `w = 2 * s * sin(theta / 2)` across all wedge angles `theta` (default `0.5 mm`). Keep `Chamfer2D.width` unchanged as its 2D horizontal leg width.
2. Increment `PROJECT_VERSION` (`61` -> `62`) and multiply legacy 3D `Deburr.width` values by `sqrt(2)` on load (the 90-degree corner ratio). Update `deburr_at_the_wall_corner_is_chamfer_byte_for_byte` to pass `w = 2.0 * sqrt(2)`.
3. Add `break_mode` (`ConstantWidth` default, `ConstantDepth`), `break_profile` (`Chamfer` default, `Round`), and multi-pass step parameters to `DeburrParams` and `OpParams::Deburr`.
4. Compute setback `s = d / cos(theta / 2)` for `ConstantDepth`. Emit outer-to-final cone chamfer passes within `EdgeBreak::floor_at`, and refuse `Round` by name on sharp cones until ball-tipped cutters run.

body:
Maintainer direction (2026-11-11): "We should aim for a high cohesion low coupling thru out our codebase as we are built crates and tests. And every gate is very costly."

Where the cost comes from today (measured 2026-11-11 on main 0e36fd14):

| Crate | Source lines | Test files (one binary each) | Depends on (workspace) |
|---|---|---|---|
| app | 72,122 | 267 | cl, geometry, motion, post, sim, tools |
| ui | 57,060 | 14 | app |
| motion | 46,643 | 65 | cl, geometry, sim, tools |
| sim | 23,444 | 50 | cl, geometry, tools |
| post | 6,181 | 5 | cl, geometry |
| geometry | 5,539 | 4 | - |
| tools | 4,306 | 1 | - |
| cl | 3,723 | 1 | - |
| kernel | 1,185 | 5 | - |

- `app` is the hub: it depends on every domain crate, so almost any change rebuilds it, and each of its 267 test files links the whole crate into its own binary.
- Tests of one domain's behaviour live in `app` (post dialect tests such as `fanuc_post`, `tormach_post`, `heidenhain_*` sit in `crates/app/tests/` while `crates/post/tests/` has 5 files), so a post-only change still builds and links `app`.
- A geometry / cl / Cargo change falls back to the batch tier.
- Each worktree's `target/` is 25-56 GB; five builds at once took the disk from 166 GB to 13 GB free on 2026-11-11.

Open questions to answer here (research, no code):
1. Fan-out: for a change in each crate, which crates and how many test binaries rebuild and relink, and how long does it take (cold and warm, with #913's cache)? One table.
2. Test placement: which `crates/app/tests/*` files test behaviour owned by post, sim, motion, cl, tools or geometry and could move to that crate with a small fixture seam instead of the whole app? Count per target crate.
3. Test binaries: what does folding a crate's test files into a few binaries (one per gate-map group) save in link time and disk, and what does it cost (`gate test <name>` selection, parallel runs, the quick tier's changed-test picking in `xtask/src/plan.rs`)?
4. Coupling: which `app` modules could become their own crate (the M4.1 seams still inside `app`: operation, project, commands, mcp, machine), and which dependencies between domain crates could be cut or inverted (motion -> sim; the new post -> tools from PR #880)?
5. Rules: which of this becomes law in AGENTS.md "Code shape" and a reviewer check (e.g. a test lives in the crate that owns the behaviour; a new dependency between workspace crates needs a decision entry; no new test file in `app` for behaviour another crate owns)?

Then file the concrete sub-issues (each with P*, effort, area, "Done means", "Part of #<this>"), ordered by gate minutes saved per unit of work, and close this umbrella.

Related: #900 / PR #913 (compile cache and lighter dev profile), #27 (kernel seam).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
